text: CPI has surged to 4.2% — a 3-year high driven by energy costs — and the Fed under new Chair Warsh is now openly considering a rate hike, which could pressure stock valuations broadly and hurt unprofitable growth names in particular.

Sell RGTI — it's down 36% and 64% off its high with declining revenue, burning cash, and 19% short interest, meaning the market is actively betting against it and the fundamentals give no reason to hold on.
Sell RDW — four straight earnings misses, negative earnings, cash-burning operations, and very high short interest add up to a broken thesis with no clear path to recovery.

Sell SGLP.L — a relative strength score of -99 means this commodity holding is performing worse than virtually everything else in the market, and sitting below its 50-day average confirms the downtrend is intact.
Trim QBTS — it's down 21% and nearly 49% off its high with no earnings, 17% short interest, and insider selling, so reducing your exposure here limits damage while the picture remains ugly.
Trim IONQ — despite impressive 202% revenue growth, the stock is deeply unprofitable with 16% short interest, and in a rising-rate environment the market punishes money-losing companies the hardest.
Raise your IONQ stop from $46.68 to $49.13 — this tightens your safety net by 5.2% so you lock in more of your remaining position if the stock drops further.

Consider adding to ADBE — a PE of 7.1 is remarkably low for a company of Adobe's quality and profitability, and if that number checks out it represents a genuinely unusual value opportunity even in a tougher rate environment.
